The tagged TestIPMTUInstalledFromNegotiatedMRU proves Ze installs ppp7 MTU 1400 from the peer's negotiated MRU, the size used by Linux IPv4 output for fragmentation; it does not send or observe an oversized IP datagram or kernel fragmentation. Delegated-boundary evidence is permitted by the repository rule and is not itself called a product defect. The existing same test carries both polarities over one 1400-MRU input; its exact-1400 assertion already excludes every value the later above-1400 loop could reject. The semantic MaxFrameLen-for-mru mutation discriminates that shared assertion but does not create a second polarity case or prove fragmentation itself. Retain the installed-MTU scoped truth and report the existing polarity-proof gap rather than silently renewing whole-pair assurance.
